claims.statement: For a supplied finite projected phase multigraph with exact integer labels for changes in selected unbounded counts, there exists an integer-valued phase potential g whose edge differences equal those labels if and only if every signed closed-walk label sum is zero. A spanning-forest propagation algorithm decides this and returns a cycle obstruction on failure. When it succeeds, U-g(z) is invariant along every represented transition.
assumptions: The finite phase vertex set and all enabled projected reaction edges are supplied or exactly enumerated.
Every edge label is the exact integer change of the selected unbounded coordinate(s).
Parallel edges are retained; projected state transitions are closed within the phase set.
claims.novelty_boundary: The potential/coboundary consistency lemma is standard graph theory. The report makes no historical-priority claim for applying it to projected reaction jumps.
costs: O(|Z|+|E|) exact arithmetic operations and storage after the finite phase graph is supplied.
Integer bit costs are charged; phase-set generation can be combinatorial and may dominate.
The criterion does not discover a useful projection or prove recurrence, closedness, or irreducibility.
claims.falsifier: For an accepted potential, any enabled transition in the stated exact graph that changes U-g(z) falsifies the graph encoding or the claimed certificate.
claims.next_gate: Audit finite-phase projection generation on broader CRNs and compare with complete integer-state reachability on matched small networks.

claims.statement: For the original one-way-core N77 network at any fixed positive rates k1,...,k5, each Gamma_n is closed, irreducible, nonexplosive, and positive recurrent. Its stationary law has phase weights proportional to (1/(2k1), 1/((n+1)k2), 1/(2(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)k3)) and an independent Pois(k4/k5) D coordinate. The family of these stationary laws is not uniformly tight inside the common linear stoichiometric plane B+C=2.
assumptions: Standard unit-volume stochastic mass-action propensities using falling factorials.
All five directional rate constants are finite and strictly positive.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, Original N77: exact reconstruction; exact_phase_check.py
claims.novelty_boundary: The pinned U entry reports the construction but omits its original proof/code packet. The present graph/rate derivation is independent reconstruction; historical novelty is not established.
costs: Exact reaction inventory, propensities, and positive rate calibration are assumed supplied.
Identifying Gamma_n requires finite phase projection plus the exact invariant label; D and A are unbounded.
Stationary burn-in and experimental sampling costs are not bounded by this analysis.
claims.falsifier: A measured enabled jump changing B+C or A-B(B+1)/2 falsifies the stated network. At n=9 and unit rates, phase frequencies (1320/1585,264/1585,1/1585) or the Pois(1) D marginal incompatible with calibrated stationary data falsify its stationary prediction.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof review and targeted prior-art search for escaping stationary families in complex-balanced stochastic CRNs.

claims.statement: The reversible four-pair completion with clamped Q activity one and all effective directional constants one has the same invariant H=A-B(B+1)/2 and classes Gamma_n. On each Gamma_n, the product of four Pois(1) weights conditioned on Gamma_n satisfies pairwise detailed balance; the resulting stationary family is not uniformly tight in B+C=2.
assumptions: Four reversible internal pairs: 2C+Q<->A+B+C, ABC+2Q<->3A+2B, 3A+2B<->2C+3Q, and 2C+Q<->2C+D.
Q is clamped at activity one; the enlarged dynamic-Q CTMC is outside scope.
Reference-volume falling-factorial propensities and all eight effective directional constants equal one.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, Reversible four-pair completion: separate audit; ../metabolic_thermo/CANDIDATE_PROOF.md; exact_phase_check.py
claims.novelty_boundary: This is separate from original N77; it adds reverse channels and a balancing chemostat. The product form and detailed-balance mechanism are established. Novelty of the escaping family is unresolved.
costs: Four internal species, one clamped balancing species, four reversible pairs, and eight directional rate constants.
High-molecularity channels, Q activity control, standard-state calibration, exact event logging, and count readout.
At n=9, approximately 4747 independent stationary snapshots are needed for at least 95 percent probability of observing phase 2 once; stationarity burn-in remains unbounded here.
No volume-limit claim; keeping B+C=2 as volume grows drives that pool concentration to zero.
claims.falsifier: Any resolved transition changing B+C or H, a persistent nonzero stationary current in a reversible pair, or phase/D frequencies incompatible with the unit-rate conditional product-Poisson law falsifies the stated model.
claims.next_gate: Independent prior-art audit and a lower-molecularity chemically grounded realization with explicit rate and chemostat acquisition.

claims.statement: In both network variants, deterministic complex-balanced dynamics have a single global attracting equilibrium on each positive class B+C=2, while stochastic classes Gamma_n have stationary laws supported on A>=n. Therefore deterministic attraction to a common limit does not imply uniform tightness of stationary stochastic laws across all communicating classes in that real stoichiometric class.
assumptions: The exact original or reversible-completion reaction graph and unit-rate mass-action models stated in FINAL_REPORT.md.
Single-linkage global-attractor theorem applies to the deterministic complex-balanced system.
The stochastic class closure, irreducibility, nonexplosion, and stationary laws established separately in RG-02 or RG-03.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, Original N77 and Reversible four-pair completion sections
claims.novelty_boundary: The counterexample is exact at model level; no claim about natural metabolism, general CRNs, or historical priority.
costs: The reaction model and all jump channels must be acquired exactly.
Family non-tightness is a cross-component quantifier; it does not refute recurrence within each component.
No general algorithm for all communicating classes or experimental realization is supplied.
claims.falsifier: A proof that the given stationary family is uniformly tight would contradict the exact support bound A>=n; for model validation, jump or stationary-frequency violations are the measurable falsifiers listed in RG-02 and RG-03.
claims.next_gate: Determine whether a biologically grounded detailed-balanced network exhibits the same phase-escape mechanism under experimentally acquired rates.

claims.statement: For a finite family rho_e=P_e/Q_e with finite rational exponent supports and strictly positive rational coefficients, the common positive denominator D=product_f Q_f lifts channel e to P_e product_(f!=e) Q_f. Its source height is h_D(w)+h_Pe(w)-h_Qe(w). Therefore the standard essential-source endotactic criterion is equivalent before and after lifting, provided neutral channels are excluded before maximizing and every active top tie is tested.
assumptions: Every P_e and Q_e has a finite nonempty support in Q^d and all coefficients are positive rational numbers; no numerator or denominator vanishes on R^d_{>0}.
Each channel has one fixed reaction vector nu_e; if coefficients vary in time, they are measurable and lie in one common compact positive interval.
The endotactic test is the essential-source condition: for each w, remove e with w dot nu_e=0, maximize source order over the remaining channels, and require every maximizer to satisfy w dot nu_e<0.
claims.novelty_boundary: Common denominator multiplication and support-function additivity are elementary; the report makes no historical novelty claim. In two species, the permanence consequence reduces to established endotactic power-law permanence after time change. The finite direct LP-cell recognizer is a transparent exponential exact formulation, not a demonstrated advantage over lifted-graph MILP.
costs: The direct all-direction procedure uses at most m*3^m*product_e(|A_e||B_e|) exact rational LP feasibility checks, each with d geometric variables and O(sum_e(|A_e|+|B_e|)+m^2) constraints.
Explicit source expansion has at most sum_e |A_e| product_(f!=e)|B_f| tuples before duplicate aggregation; exact coefficient/exponent bit growth and solver work are charged.
A real application must acquire the complete channel list, stoichiometric vectors, exact positive support representation, and bounded-rate domain; the toy assay was proposed, not run.
claims.falsifier: In the four-channel fixture, independently calibrated rate multipliers (1,1,1,2) predict net X fluxes 10322/1111 at X=10 and 100030202/1010101 at X=100. A replicated confidence interval excluding either prediction after propagating measured rate uncertainty falsifies the fixture's kinetic model; a wrong lifted source height or failed exact identity falsifies the algebra/checker implementation.
claims.next_gate: Implement the finite rational LP-cell decision procedure and compare it with an exact lifted-graph MILP on support families where the Cartesian denominator expansion dominates; then test a complete experimentally acquired rational-rate model.
